# Test fixtures

`claude/` holds fictional logs with the same layout as `~/.claude`. They are generated by `bun tests/fixtures/generate.ts` (don't edit them by hand).

- The record shapes follow a study of about 220k real records (as of 2026-10-05, Claude Code 2.1.2xx) ([builder.ts](builder.ts))
- All text, paths, PRs, etc. are fictional. Nothing from real logs is included. Conversation text may be in any language
- The time base is 2026-09-28 00:00 UTC (= 09:00 JST). "Minutes" in the table below are minutes elapsed since then

## Rules (established by the study)

| Target | Rule | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Human prompt | `type=user` and `origin.kind=human`. `promptSource` may be any of typed / suggestion_accepted / queued / sdk (sdk is input from the desktop app, etc.) | Confirmed human-typed text with `human`+`sdk` in real logs |
| Automatic-run turn | From a user record with `turnOrigin=scheduled` until the next `turnOrigin=human` (or `origin.kind=human`) | Confirmed in `/loop` sessions. Assistant records don't carry `turnOrigin`, so it is carried over as state |
| Notifications and peer | `task-notification` and `peer` don't change how a turn is treated (they inherit the previous turn) | They arrive both during human work and during automatic runs |
| Prompt-less work blocks | A block with no human prompt (or `/loop` tick) and no tool call isn't drawn: it is a compaction, an API error or a short reply to a notification after a break. Blocks without a prompt but with tool calls stay: Claude acting on a notification on its own, often with commits | In real logs (2026-10-05), 45 of 335 visible blocks had no prompt; the 9 without tool calls were all under a minute with no commits or PRs, while the 29 over a minute held 14 commits and PRs |
| SDK input | A main-thread `type=user` record with no `origin`, not `isMeta`, with `entrypoint=sdk-cli` or `promptSource=sdk`. Slash commands sent this way carry no `promptSource` | In real logs (2026-10-12), all 72 such records were in `entrypoint=sdk-cli` sessions, one per session except one with two; 69 had `promptSource=sdk` and the 3 without it were `/goal` commands |
| Headless | A session with 0 human prompts and at least one SDK input | `claude -p` has no origin and `promptSource=sdk`. Of 106 sessions with 0 human prompts, 71 came from the SDK; the rest were interactive sessions closed before any prompt (only `isMeta` records) |
| Automation or trial | Over every headless run of a launch directory: automation when they ran on more than one local day, at least 12 hours apart, or any recorded a commit, PR or merge; trial otherwise | In real logs (2026-10-16), 102 headless sessions in 22 directories: one loop in a container checkout (35 runs over 5 days, 14 with a PR) and 21 directories of probes and checks, each used on one day with nothing made |
| Title | `custom-title` > `agent-name` > `ai-title` > the first human prompt | `custom-title` is the name given with `/rename` |
| Command records without origin | E.g. records created right after `/clear`. Not counted as prompts or work blocks (the wait between `/clear` and the first prompt isn't treated as work) | Confirmed in real logs: sessions that start with `/clear` and get their first prompt over ten minutes later |
| Working directory | The `cwd` of the first record. Not changed by a later `relocated` (used only for the secondary label) | |
| Project of a headless run's directory | Without a git remote: a directory gone from this machine, or a temporary one, takes the repository of the PRs opened from it when they all point to one (and then merges like a clone); a Claude Code scratchpad (`<tmp>/claude-<uid>/<encoded launch dir>/<session>/scratchpad/…`) joins the project of the sessions launched in the directory it encodes; other temporary directories (`/tmp`, `/private/tmp`, `/var/folders`, `~/.claude/jobs/*/tmp`) belong to no project, keeping the directory name as the secondary label. So do Claude Code's configuration (`~/.claude`, except a log folder, which joins the project of the sessions it holds) and a directory that holds another project's repository (home, a folder of clones). | In real logs (2026-10-13), 10 projects held only headless runs: 4 scratchpads, 4 temporary directories, 2 container paths. Of 13 sessions in container paths, 2 carried a `pr-link`, both to the repository the others worked on. In real logs (2026-10-16), the project list still held `/tmp`, the home directory, the folder of clones, a log folder, and a copy cloned from a local clone (its origin a local path) beside the repository it came from |
| Duplicates | The same `uuid` within one session counts once | |
| Notes | `system/away_summary` and the `isCompactSummary` user record are stored as notes (`away_summary`, `compact_summary`) and never count as activity. Both appear only in the main session; the compact summary's `message.content` is a string | In real logs (2026-10-13): 555 recaps, all main-session, all with a `uuid`, written 3.0–3.2 min after the previous record (p10–p90, at most 5.8 min at p99), so counting them would stretch every block they follow. 82 compact summaries, all main-session, 12k characters at the median and up to 23k, with `Pending Tasks` and `Optional Next Step` at the end |
| PR title | The value of `--title` / `--title=` / `-t` of `gh pr create`. Linked to the PR via the result's `toolUseResult.gitOperation.pr` (`action: "created"`, number and URL) (or the PR URL in the output if there's no `gitOperation`). Values containing `$(…)` or `` ` `` are decided at run time and aren't used. If no title is available, use the `pr-link`'s "#number repository" | Neither `pr-link` (`prNumber`, `prUrl`, `prRepository`) nor `gitOperation.pr` carries a title. In real logs, 186 of 188 PR creations had `--title` or `-t`. `pr-link` comes both before and after the result (23 of 35 before) |
| PR merge | A Bash call with `gh pr merge` where a command starts (start of the call, or after `&&` / `;` / `\|` / newline, past `VAR=value` prefixes) and a result that is neither an error nor interrupted, or a result whose `toolUseResult.gitOperation.pr.action` is `merged`. The PR is the number argument (or `/pull/N` URL), else `gitOperation.pr.number`; a merge naming neither still counts once per call | In real logs (2 weeks to 2026-10-06), 122 `gh pr merge` calls succeeded but only 4 carried `gitOperation` (`{action: "merged", number}`, no URL). Merges are often run as `gh pr merge N --squash 2>&1 \| tail`, which hides failures from `is_error`, so a few failed merges may count |
| Copies in continued sessions | Records with the same `uuid` as the previous session (the one that points here via `continued-in`) are copies. Excluded from aggregates and work blocks | Confirmed in real logs that copies only have sessionId rewritten and keep the original uuid and time (all 18 `continued-in`s) |
| Token usage | `message.usage` of `type=assistant`. One response is split into per-block records sharing a `message.id`. Input and cache values are the same in every record, and `output_tokens` grows in later records, so take the maximum per `message.id`. Cache writes are split by the 5-minute / 1-hour breakdown in `usage.cache_creation` (treated as 5 minutes if there's no breakdown). `model=<synthetic>` isn't counted. A `message.id` in a continued session that matches the previous session is a copy. When `usage.iterations` is present, sum its steps instead of the top-level fields: the top level covers only `message` steps, so a server-side `compaction` step is missing from it (per the API docs), and some records zero it | In 87,421 real records / 46,428 responses (2026-10-05), input and cache values always matched within a `message.id`, and in all 7,352 responses whose `output_tokens` differed, the last record had the maximum. In 72,894 real records with `iterations` (2026-10-06), every entry was a single `message` step; the top level equalled it in 72,887 and was all 0 in 7. No `compaction` step has appeared yet: Claude Code's own `/compact` doesn't log its summarization usage |
| Effort | `effort` of `type=assistant` (high / medium). Always the same across records with the same `message.id`. A work block's effort is the value with the most output tokens | In 87,587 real records (2026-10-05), present on all but 452 (older versions). 0 responses changed value within one response |
| Claude's working time | `durationMs` of `system/turn_duration` (from the start to the end of the turn). The record's time is the end of the turn. Only present in the main session. Copied into continued sessions with the same `uuid`, so copies aren't counted. It leaves out the time the turn waited on its own AskUserQuestions, so the turn began that much before `end - durationMs`; a turn wrapping other turns (waiting on a background agent) counts wall time instead. An interrupted turn writes none | Of 2,295 in real logs, 0 were in subagent files and 124 shared a uuid with another file. In real logs (2026-10-18), of 111 turns with an AskUserQuestion answered inside, 94 begin at a request (within 2 s) once their own waits are added back (6 do without them, 11 at neither); the 37 that seemed to include their waits all wrapped another turn |
